title: 形式言語とオートマトン
subtitle: Formal Languages and Automata
teachers:
NINAGAWA Shigeru
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: Formal language is a mathematical description of a language and formal grammar is a set of rules that can be used to create sentences with a language. In this course, students learn regular language and context-free language. They also study several kinds of automata that can recognize those languages. The knowledge students learn in this course provide the foundations of the technology that processes natural languages and other languages.
advice:
In this course, students learn formal grammar and formal language, especially focusing on regular language and context-free language. They also study several kinds of automata that can recognize those languages. The topics are as follows:

1. Deterministic finite automaton
2. Nondeterministic finite automaton
3. Nondeterministic finite automaton with epsilon moves
4. Regular language
5. Regular grammar
6. Regular expression
7. Context-free grammar
8. Context-free language
9. Chomsky hierarchy
books: オートマトン・言語理論 第２版，冨田 悦次，横森 貴著，森北出版
requiredKnowledge: Review sets and their operations taken up in "Discrete mathematics", especially the notation of sets, subsets, power sets, and the direct product of sets.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain Chomsky hierarchy.
Be able to perform conversions between equivalent finite automata.
Be able to explain the definition of regular grammar and regular language.
Be able to perform conversions between regular grammar and finite automaton.
Be able to explain the definition of regular expression.
Be able to perform derivations in context-free grammar.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, students learn formal grammar and formal language, especially focusing on regular language and context-free language. They also study several kinds of automata that can recognize those languages. The topics are as follows:

1. Deterministic finite automaton
2. Nondeterministic finite automaton
3. Nondeterministic finite automaton with epsilon moves
4. Regular language
5. Regular grammar
6. Regular expression
7. Context-free grammar
